COURT OF APPEAL OF THE STATE OF WESTBROOK, DIVISION TWO

PEOPLE v. BARRETT                     No. A-160-2024-CR

APPELLANT'S REPLY BRIEF (Excerpts)

I. RESPONDENT'S ATTEMPT TO DISTINGUISH J.L. FAILS.

Respondent leans on Trooper Reeves's testimony that Appellant "seemed nervous" after a 2.4-mile follow during which he committed no traffic violation. As the U.S. Supreme Court observed in Illinois v. Wardlow, 528 U.S. 119, 124 (2000), "nervous, evasive behavior" plus presence in a high-crime area may give rise to reasonable suspicion. Nervousness alone, observed only after being followed by a marked police vehicle for over two miles, does not. See United States v. Wood, 106 F.3d 942, 948 (10th Cir. 1997) ("nervousness is of limited significance in determining reasonable suspicion").

Critically, the trooper himself testified that the stop was based "solely on the tip" (RT 94). The post-hoc invocation of "nervousness" appears for the first time in Respondent's brief.

II. McNEIL DOES NOT SUPPORT A "SELECTIVELY-WAIVED" MIRANDA REGIME.

McNeil addresses the distinction between the Sixth Amendment right to counsel (offense-specific) and the Fifth Amendment right to counsel under Miranda (NOT offense-specific). 501 U.S. at 177. The Court held that a Sixth Amendment invocation at arraignment for one offense does not bar police-initiated interrogation about a different offense. Id. at 175–176.

But Mr. Barrett was not invoking under the Sixth Amendment at arraignment. He was invoking under the Fifth Amendment, during custodial interrogation, after being given his Miranda rights. Once a suspect invokes the Fifth Amendment right to counsel during custodial interrogation, Edwards bars all further interrogation initiated by the police, on any subject, until counsel is made available. 451 U.S. at 484–485. There is no "subject-matter" exception in Edwards. McNeil did not create one.

CONCLUSION:
The trial court erred on both issues. The errors were not harmless beyond a reasonable doubt. Reversal is required.

September 12, 2024
                                /s/ A. Mercer, Esq.
